newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS-EIB pledges heavy investment in Poland.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EIB pledges heavy investment in Poland.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) is likely to double its investment in Poland to about 2.8 billion Ecus over the next three years, EIB deputy president Wolfgang Roth said on Monday.

The EIB statement released on Monday said the bank planned to contribute more than 3.5 billion Ecus to 11 Central and East European countries within the next three years and Roth later added Poland was likely to get some 40 percent of this sum.
"In the past, 40 percent of our investment in the Central and East Europe came to Poland...I think this will be the case in the future," Roth told a news conference.

He said the EIB, the European Union's investment bank, would contribute most funds to infrastructural and transportation project but that it would also invest in cement, steel and car sectors and continue to help the small business.

Roth said the EIB, which has brought to Poland 1.4 billion Ecus in favourable-term loans since the 1989 fall of communism, was reviewing loans totalling about one billion Ecus for road transport projects.
"The development of transport links is crucial for Poland's future membership in the European Union," he said.

He said the bank, which has recently granted 225 million Ecus for the contruction of a motorway linking the southern cities of Wroclaw and Gliwice, was likely to contribute another 200 million Ecus for an extension of this route.

The bank was also likely to lend between 20 and 30 percent of the 2.2 billion Ecus needed to build a motorway between Berlin and Warsaw, he said, and 200 million Ecus for regional transport projects in the cities of Krakow and Katowice.

The bank would also lend about 40 million Ecus for upgrading a railway link between the central town of Minsk Mazowiecki and Terespol on the border with Belarus and "a very high amount" for modernising a railway connection between the Baltic port of Gdansk and the Czech Republic, he said.
Roth said that along with Western companies the EIB would be a co-investor in large industrial projects, nobably in the cement, steel and car sectors.
"I cannot tell you about concrete projects...we will join west European firm in projects in Poland," he said.
Roth also said that in 1997 the bank planned to launch mid-term bonds denominated in zlotys, likely to amount to more than 100 million Ecus, to raise funds for clients who prefer to borrow in zlotys.
"We want to raise funds in zlotys...to provide them for our clients who want to avoid exchange-rate risk," he said.
He added the EIB's bond issue would be a test of whether Poland could become a long-term source of capital.
